info.name: NW-GMSA FHIR Repository & GEL Terminology Server
info.description:
Requests mirrored from notebooks/01-fhir-search-basics.ipynb, notebooks/02-work-orders-worked-example.ipynb (both against the NW-GMSA FHIR repository, {{base_url}}, HTTP Basic auth), and notebooks/13-snomed-to-hpo-genomic-clinical-indication.ipynb (against the public Genomics England terminology server, {{ontoserver}}, no auth). Requests marked "[WRITE]" are illustrative PUTs from notebook 02, section 5 — they change real Task state and are NOT executed by the notebook itself; only send them deliberately.

Every example value in folders 01/02 is a *real* identifier that either (a) is one of the NW-GMSA IG's own published genomics test patients (https://nw-gmsa.github.io/en/testing.html#genomics-test-patients), or (b) appears verbatim in one of this repo's own committed FHIR/V2 examples (which is what the FHIR repository has actually been pre-loaded with) — cross-referenced against MRN-Mapping.md. Nothing here is a made-up placeholder like "Smith" — that fictional example (from an earlier revision of this collection) does not exist in the IG or in this repo's fixtures, so it was replaced.

The chained internal-id variables (patient_id, owner_organization_id, service_request_id, specimen_ref_id, task_id, task_version_id) are pre-filled with real ids confirmed by notebooks 01/02's own already-executed live cells (captured 2026-08-26/27) rather than left blank — but a FHIR repository is mutable, so treat these as a known-good starting point, not a permanent guarantee. Each has a test script on its source request that refreshes it automatically when that request is re-run; if a chained request 404s, re-run the request that's supposed to produce that id first.

request.description: Patient?name= is a fuzzy match against Patient.name — used as a fallback after NHS number. 'Manchester' is a real published NW-GMSA IG test patient (Sansa Manchester), not a made-up name.

item.name: 2. Search Patient by date of birth

request.description: 1972-09-21 is Sansa Manchester's real DOB — same patient as request 1.

item.name: 3a. Search Patient by NHS Number (bare value)

request.description: What the app actually sends — bare value matches any identifier system. 9737383206 is LIVERPOOL, Ned, a real published IG test patient also used by notebook 02's worked example. Running this captures {{patient_id}} for the patient-scoped requests later in this folder.
system|value form for an unambiguous match.

item.name: 4. Search Patient by Medical Record Number (MRN)

request.description: Base FHIR identifier search matches on value only — filter identifier[].type.coding[].code == 'MR' client-side if needed. REM7442130 is LIVERPOOL, Ned's real Liverpool University Hospitals Trust MRN (MRN-Mapping.md).

Never run this unfiltered from user input — an unscoped Organization search can 413 this server. REN = Clatterbridge Cancer Centre, the real assigner ODS on LIVERPOOL, Ned's loaded Clatterbridge order. Running this captures {{organization_id}} for request 7a below.

None of this repo's loaded ServiceRequest examples actually carry intent=filler-order (that value shows up on Task.intent instead — see folder 02). This demonstrates the query syntax; an empty result set here is expected against the pre-loaded data, not a bug.

item.name: 6b. Search ServiceRequest by intent (order OR original-order)

request.description: Comma-joined values inside ONE intent= parameter mean OR. Two separate intent= parameters would mean AND (and always match nothing, since ServiceRequest only has one intent). Unlike 6a, this should genuinely hit loaded data — most of this repo's committed ServiceRequest examples (e.g. Liverpool_O21_Apr26.json, Clatterbridge-REN-ORU_R01.txt.json) use intent=order.

Run request 5 first to populate {{organization_id}}. Caveat: no loaded ServiceRequest example in this repo actually sets .performer, so a genuinely empty result here is expected against the pre-loaded data — this demonstrates the query shape, not a guaranteed hit.

Chained search support varies by server — fall back to a two-step Practitioner lookup + performer=<id> if this comes back empty unexpectedly. 'Iqbal' is a real requesting Practitioner (Shahid Iqbal) on LIVERPOOL, Ned's loaded Clatterbridge order — note that example sets ServiceRequest.requester, not .performer, so this chained performer search may still come back empty against the pre-loaded data even though the Practitioner itself is real.

Same pattern works for DiagnosticReport?identifier= too — try both when you can't tell which kind of number you have. CB-260817-01 is LIVERPOOL, Ned's real Placer Order Number, assigner REN, from Output/FHIR/R01/Clatterbridge-REN-ORU_R01.txt.json.

item.name: 9. Search ServiceRequest by authored date range (ge/le)

request.description: Repeated authored= parameters here mean AND (contrast with intent's comma-for-OR above). Full-year 2026 range chosen to cover this repo's own loaded ServiceRequest.authoredOn examples, which span 2026-01 through 2026-08.
S26-1K1Q is a real Specimen identifier from the NW-GMSA IG's own published ctDNA example (patient SHEFFIELD, Theon).

Same S26-1K1Q value, but this one genuinely IS tagged with this exact system in the source example (Input/FHIR/NWGMSA-Examples/O21/Bundle-GenomicsOrderMessage-ctDNA.json), unlike the made-up specimen used in an earlier revision of this collection.
Run request 3a first (or set {{patient_id}} manually) — this is the internal FHIR id for LIVERPOOL, Ned, not his NHS number.

item.name: 2. Find work orders (Task, filler-order, requested, owned by lab)

exec: console.log('No requested filler-order Task found for this owner — nothing to chain into request 3a/5a/5b.');

request.description: Matches FhirClient.active_filler_tasks(). Deliberately scoped by owner (never system-wide) to avoid the 413s an unscoped query can trigger. Task resources aren't part of this repo's static example files — they're expected to exist live in the FHIR repository as a side effect of the pre-loaded orders having actually been processed by the RIE. Running this auto-captures {{task_id}}, {{task_version_id}} and {{service_request_id}} for the requests below.

exec: console.log('patient_id set to ' + parts[1] + ' from ServiceRequest.subject');

request.description: A plain FHIR read (Task.focus target) — returns the resource itself, not a searchset Bundle. Order Filler Number = identifier[] typed 'FILL'; Order Placer Number = typed 'PLAC'. Auto-captures {{specimen_ref_id}} and {{patient_id}} for the requests below.

From a specimen reference on the ServiceRequest above (ServiceRequest.specimen[]) — {{specimen_ref_id}} is the internal FHIR id captured by request 3a, distinct from the business identifier used in folder 01's {{specimen_id}}.
From ServiceRequest.subject, captured by request 3a.

item.name: 4. Search RelatedPerson by patient (mother of fetus/baby)

request.description: For a fetus/baby Patient with no NHS number yet — the mother's own demographics are carried directly on the RelatedPerson resource. relationship.coding[].code is expected to be HL7 v3 RoleCode MTH/NMTH, but this is unconfirmed against this server. This repo's own fetus/baby fixtures (e.g. Input/V2/O21/OML_O21_R0A_FetusOfCersei_R22.1.txt, ...BabyOfGilly..., ...BabyOfLysa..., ...BabyOfBrienne...) are a better fit for exercising this than the {{patient_id}} chained from LIVERPOOL, Ned above, who is an adult.

NOT executed by notebook 02 (illustrative only). This app has no button for this yet — moving a real Task to 'accepted' has real downstream workflow consequences. Replace the body with the full Task fetched from request 2 above, with only .status changed, before ever sending this for real. If-Match uses Task.meta.versionId for optimistic concurrency (expect 412 Precondition Failed on a stale version).
NOT executed by notebook 02 (illustrative only). Task.statusReason carries the why, separate from status itself — worth populating on rejected/cancelled transitions.

item.name: 13 - Genomics England Terminology Server (SNOMED <-> HPO)
item.description: https://re-docs.genomicsengland.co.uk/terminology_server — public, no auth required. Overrides the collection's Basic Auth with noauth on every request here since {{ontoserver}} isn't this repo's own FHIR_SERVER.

request.description: Confirms reachability. Unlike this repo's own FHIR_SERVER, no Authorization header is needed here — expect 200.

item.name: 2a. CodeSystem $lookup — confirm a SNOMED code is real (finding)

request.description: Returns a Parameters resource with the concept's real display term, or an OperationOutcome if the code doesn't exist. $translate alone can't distinguish a made-up code from a real one with no mapping — $lookup is the way to tell them apart first.

Verified live 2026-09-06: returns HTTP 404 (not 200) with an OperationOutcome body — issue[0].code="not-found". The notebook's own check (resourceType == "OperationOutcome") still works since requests.json() parses the body regardless of status code, but a raise_for_status()-style check would need to tolerate 404 here specifically.

item.name: 3a. ValueSet $validate-code — real code, any SNOMED concept

request.description: "Is this a real code at all" — result=true expected for a genuine SNOMED CT concept.
An ECL expression for descendants of 404684003 'Clinical finding'. Ataxia (20262006) is a member — expect result=true.
Appendectomy (80146002) is a real, valid SNOMED code — just a Procedure, not a Clinical finding descendant. Expect result=false: a different kind of 'invalid' than a made-up code.
For NOS/HPOTerm on Questionnaire-GMSWGSRareDisease.html. Clinical signs/findings (Ataxia here) translate cleanly to HPO.

item.name: 4b. ConceptMap sct-to-hpo $translate — SNOMED diagnosis -> HPO (no mapping)

request.description: Lynch syndrome (716318002) is a named diagnosis, not a single phenotype — result=false expected. Not a coverage gap: a disease implies many possible HPO terms, so there's nothing single-valued for $translate to return.

For writing an HPO-coded genomic finding back into a SNOMED-native EPR problem list. Same ConceptMap, reverse=true inverts direction — no separate hpo-to-sct map needed. HP:0001251 (Ataxia) round-trips back to sct_finding_code exactly. Expect an informational 'ignored target scope' warning in the response — not a sign the match is wrong.

item.name: 5b. ConceptMap sct-to-hpo $translate reverse — HPO -> SNOMED (no mapping)

request.description: HP:0001519 'Disproportionate tall stature' — a real, valid HPO term (associated with Marfan syndrome), but not in the map. Contrast with 5a's hpo_maps_code (HP:0001166 Arachnodactyly), which does map — coverage needs checking per code, not assumed from the sign/diagnosis pattern alone.

item.name: 6. List every ConceptMap published on this server

request.description: Confirms there is no sct-to-genomic-clinical-indication (or similar) map for OBR-31's CodeSystem-GenomicClinicalIndication — only four ConceptMaps exist on this server today, none targeting it. Checked by listing, not assumed from docs silence.
